scope: Strategic RAID register for the DAS Technology (Digital Air Strike) CDP Phase 0 engagement. Risks and Assumptions are the core register and live only here. Issues and Dependencies are summarized at a strategic level; tactical tracking lives in GitHub (ConflictHQ/das-tech) and the open-questions / action-items trackers.

items.title: Golden record may not be achievable from DAS's real data
items.detail: The engagement's central question (Mike Paylor): 'Is it possible to take all the data we have and make a golden record for myself, and what would that even look like?' DAS has zero cross-system identity resolution today ('We don't'), and the only existing join key (Common Client ID) is recent, low-investment, and already showing cleanliness issues. If the source data cannot support deterministic + probabilistic resolution at acceptable quality, the core premise of the CDP is at risk. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.owner: Alicia Salazar / Luis Hernandez (real-data proof); Leo Mata (review)
items.mitigation: Prove identity resolution against actual data, not schemas ('all the people that could be Mike'). Build the golden-record portal view as the validation artifact. Identity strategy options due ~2026-06-19; war-room design sessions feed the proof.

items.title: Common Client ID quality is unproven and may not serve as a reliable migration/backfill key
items.detail: Common Client ID is the current cross-source join key but was recently implemented with data-cleanliness issues already discovered. It is treated as one candidate deterministic signal and the historical migration/backfill join, not the identity foundation. If CCID coverage is sparse or dirty, historical backfill and any deterministic weighting degrade. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.owner: CONFLICT (audit, self-serve via DWRPT access); Ron Mulder (ID-assignment logic)
items.mitigation: CCID audit underway via granted DWRPT read access. Identity design is first-principles and does not gate on CCID, so a poor result reduces (not blocks) the design. Per-source identity-signal inventory reduces reliance on any single key.

items.title: Acceptor event payloads may carry post-processed records rather than raw inbound data
items.detail: The direct-from-source ingestion thesis assumes the CDP can capture raw events at the point of consumption (e.g., DAS Acceptor publishes a CRM lead to the Event Bus). If those event payloads are already post-processed rather than the raw inbound lead, the data-manipulation problem the client distrusts simply moves one layer upstream. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.mitigation: Open session topic to confirm whether Acceptor (and other publishers) emit raw vs processed payloads. CDP event intake stays bus-agnostic with per-bus adapters, so the channel design holds regardless; payload shape is what needs confirming.

items.title: DAS-side event delivery is real engineering that may not be deliverable on the Phase-1 timeline
items.detail: The decided event-delivery design (Option A) needs DAS to add an Event Grid event-subscription pointed at the CDP webhook (config-only on their side). Direct-publish (Option B) is acknowledged as 'tough' and real DAS-side engineering. The DAS-owned Event Grid subscription is a monitored critical-path dependency; if DAS does not own/operate it reliably, the live event feed is at risk. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.mitigation: Design Option A as production-grade / possibly permanent. Contract DAS to publish CloudEvents 1.0 so a future Option B is a config swap, not a rewrite. Data Source Status portal surface alerts on event-feed liveness; ownership documented with DAS.

items.title: Dev environment points at production databases
items.detail: Flagged as a critical current-state condition: DAS dev currently points to production databases. Must be corrected before any build begins; left unaddressed it is a data-integrity and safety hazard for Phase 1. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.mitigation: Listed under 'What NOT to build on' and as a Phase-1 prerequisite. No CONFLICT build work proceeds against production-pointed dev.
items.source: memory/decisions.md (What NOT to build on), memory/open-questions.md (Still open)

items.title: Field Catalog v1 (the initial 27) misread as the finished data model
items.detail: The 27 MVP data points are the bare-minimum MVP floor, explicitly not the data model or the design target. There is a standing risk that stakeholders (or our own framing) treat 'the 27' as a closed, complete model and under-scope the record. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.mitigation: Renamed Field Catalog v1; versioned and grows. Always say 'Field Catalog v1 (the initial 27)', never 'the 27-point model'. Expansion candidates accrue in docs/cdp-field-source-matrix.md and graduate per version.

items.title: Redshift + zero-ETL is the costliest portability swap-point
items.detail: The proposed analytics tier uses Redshift via zero-ETL from RDS-Postgres. Of all AWS-proprietary choices, Redshift is called out as the priciest swap if portability weight rises (the portable alternative is analytics-native Postgres / Synapse). A later mandate to move off AWS would make this the heaviest rework. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.mitigation: Isolate proprietary services behind interfaces; no vendor lock-in in app code. Redshift flagged as the one to revisit if portability weight rises. Open/non-blocking item.

items.title: Cross-store PII erasure propagation (crypto-shred risk, superseded by PII vault)
items.detail: Crypto-shred (per-consumer DEK key destruction) gives right-to-erasure over the append-only/bitemporal store, but only if no plaintext PII escapes the encryption boundary and the erasure propagates to every PII copy: S3 bronze, Redshift, OpenSearch, and caches. KMS economics are trivial; the boundary and propagation are the real work. SUPERSEDED 2026-06-21: the tokenized PII vault (delete-the-row) dissolves this risk - PII lives only in the vault; downstream stores (S3 bronze, analytics, OpenSearch) hold tokens that dereference to nothing, so there is nothing to propagate. CLOSED 2026-06-18: documented and accepted as a known risk — carried into the Phase 0 deliverables risk register (Executive Summary / Scoping Doc); no open Phase-0 action.
items.owner: CONFLICT (mechanism); Alicia Salazar + Luis Hernandez (privacy policy)
items.mitigation: Options catalogued in docs/consent-pii-erasure-options.md (envelope encryption, DynamoDB vs Postgres keystore, isolated-Redis DEK cache, Lambda/Temporal cleanup orchestration). Mechanism built as Phase-1 stories; policy gated to the Privacy-by-Design deliverable.

items.title: CDP ingests from original sources, never from EDW/DWRPT/SSIS outputs
items.detail: Working assumption (client-validated unprompted): the CDP captures raw data at the point of consumption from the original feeds, because DAS does not trust CDXP/SSIS data manipulation. The CDP replaces EDW; DWRPT is a reporting-parity reference only, not an ingestion source.

items.title: The CDP becomes the source of truth and the legacy SSIS/CDXP stack retires
items.detail: Reaffirmed at exec level (Dan Aston, Mike Paylor): every source that moves onto the CDP is an SSIS job that can be killed; apps, agentic features, and end-user capabilities build on top of the CDP. We assume legacy systems are context, never foundation ('replace, don't improve'). Mike: don't spend time figuring out how to redo the legacy system.

items.title: Identity resolution and reporting are first-principles CONFLICT designs
items.detail: DAS is asking CONFLICT to design identity resolution precisely because they have not solved it. We assume we do NOT anchor schema or strategy on Common Client ID or any DAS identity work, and we do NOT replicate Juicebox. CCID = one candidate signal + migration key. The 14 CDXP-Live reports are acceptance criteria, not design templates.

items.title: Ingestion is generic event intake + Airflow batch over one shared pipeline
items.detail: Assumed design: a bus-agnostic event subscription channel (per-bus adapters for Event Grid / Service Bus / Kafka / EventBridge) plus Airflow batch, sharing one validate to normalize to resolve pipeline, so sources graduate from batch to events without redesign. DAS's Azure Event Grid is the likely first adapter, never a coupling.

items.title: Cloud target under decision — Azure-primary preference, AWS-vs-Azure bake-off pending
items.detail: Phase-0 architecture recommendation (directional, not a build commitment): build on AWS for data gravity (source DBs on EC2/RDS), team tooling, self-contained home. Reusing DAS's Kong (cross-cloud to Azure) is off the table. Keep the core portable to Azure/AKS with minor changes; isolate AWS-proprietary swap-points behind interfaces. UPDATED 2026-06-18: the AWS-native directional assumption was overtaken by Dan Aston’s 2026-06-17 Azure-primary preference. No flip — now a client choice pending the AWS-vs-Azure bake-off (docs/cloud-aws-vs-azure-bakeoff.md). Target = Azure AKS + Postgres, portable OSS core self-hosted. CLOSED 2026-06-18: not a CONFLICT-side open decision. We present both AWS and Azure cases (the bake-off, docs/cloud-aws-vs-azure-bakeoff.md) and DAS chooses; the Architecture Plan is written to accommodate the decision.

items.title: PostgreSQL + row-level security is the leading-contender multi-tenancy mechanism
items.detail: Working assumption: native RDS for PostgreSQL (not Aurora) + RLS as the canonical model, serving, and tenant isolation (resolver role above tenant RLS for DAS-global identity; attributes/events dealer-isolated; bitemporal provenance carries valid-time + system-time). RLS is the leading contender, not locked: the privacy/tenancy isolation mechanism is owned by the privacy-by-design design (Alicia + Luis) and may be refined. Erasure is the tokenized PII vault (delete-the-row); RLS (access control) and the vault (erasure) are orthogonal and compose. Per-consumer DEK/crypto-shred superseded 2026-06-21; optional salt+pepper is at-rest defense-in-depth only. CONFIRMED 2026-06-18: PostgreSQL row-level security adopted as the multi-tenancy mechanism (Alicia’s multi-tenant architecture strategy; decisions.md). Settled as the working design — refinements are build-time detail, not an open question.

items.title: Phase 0 is a fixed-scope, ~1-month, documents-only discovery with CDP document before July 4
items.detail: Assumed scope and timeline: Phase 0 is ~1 month, started 2026-05-27, no code and no infra, three deliverables (Executive Summary, Revised CDP Architecture Plan, DAS CDP Roadmap). Currently week 2 of 4; one more week of discovery then wrap. Delivery before July 4 (target end of June), drafts shared early. CONFIRMED 2026-06-18: Phase 0 scope is well documented (bootstrap.md §3, PROCESS.md, kickoff) — a settled fact, not an open assumption.

items.title: Orphan identifiers and consent/suppression are first-class data categories
items.detail: Assumed by design: identifiers with nothing to join to today (e.g., Facebook IDs from reviews) are stored, attributed, and resolvable later, never discarded. Consent/suppression data (unsubscribes, suppression lists, GLBA flags) is a CDP data-model category in its own right, authoritative before any activation use.
items.owner: CONFLICT (identity + privacy design); Dan Aston (edge case source)

items.title: Auth0 is the primary identity provider, federating EntraID
items.detail: Assumed (DAS-approved): Auth0 as primary auth (SaaS, federates EntraID), Cognito as AWS-native fallback; 4-role group-based model (das_admin / das_analyst / dealer_admin / dealer_user). Recorded as a resolved CDP architecture decision.

items.title: API usage coverage per third-party integration is not yet visible
items.detail: Strategic issue: for the catalogued third-party APIs (ad platforms, comms, DMS/CRM, enrichment, reviews, billing), CONFLICT has mapped products from the Integration Explorer but lacks visibility into what DAS actually extracts TODAY vs what each API offers for future integration. This gates which fields the CDP must cover at launch vs later. Dan Aston took the list to engineering. Tactical tracking and the full API list live in GitHub and docs/api-integration-catalog.md. RESOLVED 2026-06-18 (PR #121): DAS engineering walkthrough delivered per-API business purpose + active endpoints; CDP field-coverage targets set.
items.owner: DAS Engineering / Product (walkthrough); CONFLICT (Hiram Gonzalez, Byron Miranda, Julio Rojas, Oscar Morera)
items.mitigation: Confirmed answers land in docs/api-integration-catalog.md; Dan chasing the engineering walkthrough in parallel.

items.title: Six CDP architecture design questions need direction before they harden
items.detail: Strategic issue surfaced 2026-06-13 when validating the CDP stack against Dan/Mike. RESOLVED 2026-06-21 — all six design items are routed/locked: survivorship/source-trust ranking (LOCKED 2026-06-17, DMS ground-truth + per-field matrix), household/family resolution (LOCKED 2026-06-18), bitemporal/provenance schema shapes (LOCKED 2026-06-18, tstzrange + GiST), consent enforcement model (consent taxonomy APPROVED 2026-06-19; consent store + hash-chained ledger specced), AI/agentic readiness (dual REST+GraphQL surface + AI-context schema specced), and the config-driven source registry (source_registry specced). Residual is NOT an open design question: the consent *policy values* (retention periods, taxonomy detail, lawful basis) are a Privacy-by-Design deliverable item owned by Alicia + Luis with DAS Legal (Legal approves at proposal stage, not a Phase-0 blocker). Consistent with memory/open-questions.md (no open Phase-0 design questions).

items.title: API edge gateway is an open decision (Kong vs ALB)
items.detail: The API ingress/edge for the CDP (REST + GraphQL + event webhook) is an open architecture decision: ALB (near-zero ops, AWS-native, but not an API gateway) vs a self-hosted Kong gateway (per-consumer keys, rate limits/quotas, transformation, dev portal, at the cost of another control+data plane). Driver: how API-product-like the external surface is (M2M ingestion auth, dealer/external API exposure, activation) vs ops appetite. Reusing DAS's own Kong (cross-cloud to Azure) stays off the table. CLOSED 2026-06-18: not a now-decision. Edge gateway (Kong vs ALB) is a Phase-1 build choice, not a Phase-0 blocker; deferred.
items.mitigation: Options in docs/api-edge-gateway-options.md; phasing option to ship ALB now and add Kong behind it later (additive). Logged as an open decision in memory/decisions.md.
items.source: memory/decisions.md (API ingress / edge gateway, reopened 2026-06-14), docs/api-edge-gateway-options.md

items.title: Common Client ID schema + sample extract and ID-assignment logic (Ron Mulder)
items.detail: Strategic dependency: the only remaining data dependency that materially informs the identity-resolution design. Does not gate the first-principles design but sets CCID's weight as a candidate signal and the migration/backfill path. Monitored critical-path dependency for the event-driven ingestion channel. CLOSED 2026-06-18: not needed now. Event intake is bus-agnostic by design; the Event Grid catalog/subscription is figured out collaboratively at Phase-1 build time, not a Phase-0 dependency.

items.title: Dealer-tenant scale (~1,700) used for cost/scale models is unconfirmed and conflicts with DAS's published 9,200+ footprint
items.detail: The ~1,700 dealer figure drives the cost, scale, and per-seat modeling in four deliverables (executive-summary.md, privacy-by-design-framework.md, services-topology.md, reporting-data-flow.md). DAS's public marketing cites 9,300+ dealerships/partners and 9,200+ retailers; the only public '1,700' is the sample size of DAS's 2025 NADA Lead Response Study, not a tenant count. If 1,700 is the intended initial pilot/CDP-cohort scope the models are sound; if it stands in for total tenancy, cost/scale/per-seat models are ~5x under-sized. Surfaced by the 2026-06-24 repo hallucination sweep; pending client confirmation. RESOLVED 2026-06-30 — Decision (Leo Mata): tenant count is not a blocker and does not gate the architecture. The CDP is designed to support both the ~1,700 pilot-cohort and the full ~9,200+ footprint — multi-tenant RLS plus per-tenant partitioning scale across that range without redesign. The cost/scale/per-seat figures in the four deliverables are illustrative at the modeled cohort size and re-parameterize by tenant count without architectural change; they will be re-stated against the confirmed cohort when DAS sets Phase 1 scope. No re-sizing is required to proceed.
items.owner: Leo Mata (confirm with DAS — Mike Paylor / Dan Aston)
items.mitigation: Confirm with DAS whether ~1,700 is the intended pilot/CDP-cohort scope or a stand-in for total tenancy (~9,200+). If total, re-size the cost/scale/per-seat models across the four deliverables before they are relied upon.

items.title: Golden record self-contradicts on verification: 4 source_mappings carry verified=true with disputing notes; 'zero verified=false' headline is false
items.detail: record.json's changelog hardened all 11 soft source_mappings to verified=true ('zero verified=false'), but 4 of them keep notes that say the opposite — e.g. the email-event webhook mapping is verified=true with note 'grep token too generic to confirm — honest verified=false'; same on the Conversion-feedback EMQ, Ad-interactions gclid, and Lead Ads/Messenger mappings. So the locked v1.0 sign-off's 'all 55 materialized attrs verified / zero verified=false' is false against the record's own data. Surfaced by the 2026-06-24 hallucination sweep. Deliberately NOT auto-fixed: whether each of the 4 is genuinely verified is a data-owner judgment, not a mechanical edit. RESOLVED 2026-06-30 — checked all 4 mappings (Meta EMQ, SendGrid event webhook, Meta Lead Ads/Messenger, Google gclid) against their cited vendor research pages and confirmed each field is documented there (wiki:meta / wiki:sendgrid / wiki:google-ads). The stale 'honest verified=false' notes were an artifact of the grep running against DAS internal DDL, which never contains external vendor-API fields. verified=true = present in the cited vendor page (not per-consumer-ingested by DAS today); rewrote the 4 notes to cite the wiki page as the evidence and aligned record.json status + changelog. No per-person verification is asserted.
items.owner: Alicia Salazar (golden-record owner; with Luis Hernandez)
items.mitigation: Reconcile the 4 disputed source_mappings in analysis/artifacts/golden-record/record.json — either set them back to verified=false or rewrite the notes to match — then the 'zero verified=false' headline becomes true; align record.json status and REVIEW.md to the reconciled state.
